title: Movement Patterns: Push & Pull

learn.summary: Upper-body training reduces to pushing things away and pulling things toward you, horizontally and vertically. Modern life is push-dominant and pull-starved, which is why rounded shoulders are everywhere — bias your pulling volume at roughly 2:1 over pushing until posture and shoulder health say otherwise.

do: Do one push session and one pull session this week — even 3 sets each of push-ups and rows counts.

children.title: Push Progressions

learn.summary: The push-up scales beautifully in both directions: wall → countertop → knees → full → feet-elevated → one-arm progressions. Move up a level when you can do 3 sets of 12 with a rigid plank body and full range. Elevating your hands is not cheating — it's exactly how load is supposed to be managed.

do: Find your current push-up level (the one where you can do 8–12 clean reps) and do 3 sets of it twice this week.

children.title: Pull Progressions

learn.summary: Rows come before pull-ups: inverted rows under a sturdy table or with a suspension trainer let you scale difficulty just by changing body angle. For most adults the arc is table rows → low-bar rows → band-assisted pull-ups → dead-hang pull-ups. A first strict pull-up typically requires being able to row your bodyweight horizontally for 8+ reps and dead-hang for 30+ seconds.

do: Do 3 sets of 8 rows this week using a sturdy table edge, backpack rows, or resistance band — pick whatever is available.

children.title: Push/Pull Balance

learn.summary: Count your weekly sets: if pushing (push-ups, presses, bench) outnumbers pulling (rows, pull-ups, face pulls), you're feeding the desk-hunch pattern. Aim for at least as many pull sets as push sets — 2:1 pull-biased if you sit all day. Rear-delt and mid-back work is the cheapest posture insurance available.

do: Audit last week's training (or plan this week's): count push sets vs pull sets and adjust until pulls are at least equal.

children.title: Overhead Work

learn.summary: Pressing overhead demands shoulder mobility most adults have lost — test by standing back against a wall and raising straight arms overhead to touch it without the ribs flaring. If you pass, light overhead pressing and hanging from a bar are superb shoulder maintenance; if not, earn the range first with wall slides and lat stretches.

do: Do the wall overhead-reach test today; if you pass, accumulate 60 seconds of dead-hangs this week — if not, do wall slides 3 times.
